prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 2015 manifesto (policy-focused, non-ideological)

Economic and fiscal policy
- Endorses modest year-on-year increases in public spending alongside falling deficit/debt as a share of income.
- Prioritises infrastructure investment (transport, energy, digital, housing) to boost productivity and jobs.
- Seeks a sovereign wealth fund from future energy revenues.
- Revenue measures: restore 50p top income tax rate; levy on banks and bankers’ bonuses; property tax on £2m+ homes; curb tax avoidance/evasion; abolish “non‑dom” status; review pension tax relief for highest earners; consider tobacco levy.
- Targeted business support: expand export finance; strengthen prompt-payment rules; maintain/extend Annual Investment Allowance; raise Employment Allowance to £6,000 by 2019–20; seed‑fund a Scottish Business Development Bank.

Jobs, pay and welfare
- Raise the UK minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; increase youth and apprentice rates; promote the Living Wage through procurement and accreditation.
- Reform welfare: abolish the bedroom tax; halt and review Universal Credit and PIP rollout; increase work allowance by 20%; uprate benefits at least by cost of living; raise Carer’s Allowance to Jobseeker’s Allowance level; review sanctions/conditionality and disability assessments.
- Protect pensioners: retain triple lock; support single‑tier pension at £160/week; review rise in state pension age beyond 66; keep Winter Fuel Allowance and Savings Credit.

Public services and households
- Health: increase UK health spending (implying £2bn more for Scotland by 2020–21); protect services from privatisation; invest in mental health, integration of health and social care, delayed discharge reduction, specialist nursing, and access to new medicines.
- Education/skills: 30 hours/week free nursery education for all 3–4-year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds; 30,000 Modern Apprenticeships annually; expand Education Maintenance Allowance; maintain free university tuition; targeted attainment funding.
- Housing: support a UK target of 100,000 affordable homes annually; additional capital for Scottish housebuilding.
- Energy bills: fund the Energy Company Obligation from general taxation; empower regulators to ensure wholesale price cuts are passed to consumers; fair pricing for prepayment users; earlier Winter Fuel payments for off‑grid homes.

Industry and regions
- Oil and gas: implement supportive fiscal/regulatory actions; deploy the Oil and Gas Authority; strengthen supply‑chain and internationalisation.
- Transport and digital: connect Scotland to HS2 and develop a high‑speed link with northern England; accelerate superfast broadband and 4G rollout; apply a telecoms/broadband Universal Service Obligation.
- Tourism/aviation: devolve and cut Air Passenger Duty by 50% then abolish; consider VAT reduction for hospitality.
- Cities and rural: extend City Deals; create a Scottish Cities Fund; protect Royal Mail’s Universal Service and retain/expand public stake; fairer rural fuel pricing; full devolution of food levies; secure fair share of CAP convergence uplift.

Energy, climate, and environment
- Maintain moratorium on fracking.
- Expand renewables: adjust Contracts for Difference for offshore wind; continue onshore wind support; back hydro, pumped storage, CCS; remove grid and transmission barriers; grow community energy and heat; extend Renewable Heat Incentive.
- Support species protection and action against illegal wildlife trade.

Constitution, rights, and governance
- Seek enhanced devolution: rapid delivery of Smith proposals; move toward full fiscal responsibility; devolve employment policy (including minimum wage), welfare, business taxes, National Insurance, equality policy; greater international/EU representation for devolved matters; retain Barnett during transition.
- Electoral and institutional reform: effective MP recall; proportional voting (STV) for Commons; replace the House of Lords with an elected chamber; votes at 16–17.
- Civil liberties and media: oppose mass data retention; support targeted, overseen powers; devolve broadcasting; increase BBC Scotland funding share; protect NHS/Scottish Water from TTIP; set Scotland-specific listed sporting events.
- Equality and human rights: enforce gender pay gap reporting; increase women’s representation on public boards; tighten maternity discrimination law; create a Race Committee; review immigration detention; remove VAT on sanitary products; retain Human Rights Act and ECHR commitments.

Defence and foreign policy
- Oppose renewal of the UK’s nuclear deterrent; publish full costs.
- Strengthen conventional capability in Scotland (maritime patrol aircraft, patrol vessels); transparency in defence spend/procurement; build Type 26 frigates in Scotland; improve safety systems and support for service personnel and veterans.
- International: maintain 0.7% GNI for aid (non‑defence use); audit developing country debt; appoint an envoy for global LGBTI rights; support a two‑state solution for Israel/Palestine.

EU and migration
- Support continued EU membership; propose “double‑majority” referendum rule by nation; expand devolved participation in EU decision‑making; retain free movement; participate in the European Arrest Warrant.
- Reinstate a post‑study work visa in Scotland.
